colors.role: Primary brand red - headings (h2/h4), .bkgRed backgrounds (top promo strip), .red text, red-left-border accents. The core Ville de Lausanne / SiL identity color.
Darker red, hover/active state of the primary red family (buttons, links).
Secondary red shade, used in gradients/hover states alongside #e1313c.

CTA green. Not in the static CSS bundle - injected per-button as an inline <style> override (`#cta-button-<uuid>{background-color:#09a16d}`) on every 'nativa'/energy-choice call-to-action across all universes (electricite, chaleur, gaz, raccordement...). This is the de-facto 'act now' action color across the whole SiL section, distinct from the red used by the rest of lausanne.ch.
Interactive blue - .lien buttons, focus/selection outlines (.is-selected), secondary links.
Lighter accent blue, hover states of the interactive blue.
Amber/orange accent, used sparingly for warnings/highlights.

colorsExcludedAsNonBrand.reason: JS variable for an active map-marker icon color, not a UI/brand color.
JS variable for an inactive map-marker icon color, not a UI/brand color.
Windows tile meta color (msapplication-TileColor), Microsoft-tile default, not part of the visual design.
Safari pinned-tab mask-icon color meta tag, not part of the visual design.
One-off inline table cell highlight on a single editorial tariff table (particuliers-gaz-naturel), not a reusable design token.

typography.notes: Single typeface (Open Sans) for the whole site, self-hosted as woff2/woff under /.resources/.../fonts/. No secondary/display typeface was found.

notes: The SiL sub-site reuses lausanne.ch's global Bootstrap-based design system (main.min.css, ~770KB unminified selectors incl. full Bootstrap 5 reset) rather than having its own dedicated stylesheet.

There is no per-universe (electricite/gaz/chaleur/multimedia/mobilite) color coding in the CSS: every CTA button uses the same green (#09a16d) regardless of universe, and category icons (acces-direct) are plain single-color inline SVGs (currentColor), not hex-coded per category.

The CTA green (#09a16d) is the single most actionable finding for a redesign: it is applied ad-hoc via inline <style> blocks per button instance rather than a CSS class, suggesting content editors pick it manually each time - a real design-system opportunity.
